co_snake_buttress.blurb: Snake Buttress is a granite buttress among the Cathedral Spires, in the South Platte country southwest of Denver, sitting at roughly 7,300 feet. Around sixteen routes share it, a blend of bolted slab lines and a few crack climbs, with a small number of top-rope options. Difficulty runs from about 5.8 into the low 5.12 range, and the bulk of the climbs sit at 5.10. Expect real trad craft on the cracks and careful footwork on the slabs. The walk in follows an old gated road up a drainage and is longer and steeper than it appears; cairns help you find the second big rock, which is this one.

co_wall_of_winter_warmth.blurb: Wall of Winter Warmth is a granite wall in Lower Dream Canyon, in Boulder Canyon west of Boulder, at about 7,300 feet and probably the tallest rock in that gorge. Climbs reach as many as four pitches. Most of the sixteen routes are trad, with a few bolted lines, ranging from easy ground and 5.8 up to a single 5.13. Five routes sit in the 5.12 grade, so there is plenty for strong climbers. The stone is steep and featured, and the lower section by the creek holds short, high-quality cracks. Watch for loose flakes and bird droppings in places, and for hikers and anglers below.

co_three_amigos_the.blurb: The Three Amigos are a trio of large south-facing granite outcrops tucked into a valley above Davis Meadow, behind Davis Face, near Buena Vista in the Arkansas River Valley. This is a quiet trad destination with fifteen routes, mostly two to four pitches and commonly 200 to 500 feet long. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.10, with most lines at 5.7 to 5.9, so it suits parties comfortable on moderate multi-pitch terrain. Cracks, corners and natural chimneys dominate, and some pitches are run-out. The open south face heats quickly in the high-country sun, so early or late starts are pleasant.

co_five_and_dime_boulders.blurb: Five and Dime Boulders is a bouldering sector in Castlewood Canyon, south of Denver near Castle Rock. It is a spread-out hillside of blocks, set apart from the busier parts of the canyon and quiet by comparison. The fifteen problems here run from V0 to V7, with most in the easy-to-moderate V0 to V2 range and a handful of harder lines above. A few are highballs with a poor landing, and the cliff above, around 25 to 30 feet tall in spots, also has traverses and some roped climbing. Lichen-streaked faces and aretes are typical, and some faces look north, keeping them cooler.

co_lower_east_face.blurb: The Lower East Face is the broad band of less-than-vertical rock beneath Longs Peak's upper east side, in Rocky Mountain National Park at about 13,500 feet. All fifteen routes here are alpine-style, mostly long multi-pitch trad climbs of three to seven pitches, with grades from easy scrambling and moderate fifth class up to the 5.12 range, most of them from 5.8 to 5.12. In autumn and winter it also holds some serious mixed and ice lines. The east-facing wall goes into shade by early afternoon in summer. The approach is a long hike past Chasm Lake, and falling rock and ice are real hazards.

co_monkey_skull_the.blurb: The Monkey Skull is a large quartz monzonite plate in the South Fork of St. Vrain Canyon, west of Lyons, and one of the most popular stops in that canyon. It faces west, so it picks up afternoon sun, with a short, steep walk from the road. The fifteen climbs mix moderate trad and sport lines, plus a couple of boulder problems. Almost everything falls at 5.10, with a few easier and one harder route, and the cracks, dihedrals and overhangs are where the trad shines. This is also where sport climbing in the canyon got its start. Some loose rock sits near a few of the starts.

co_pirate_s_cove.blurb: Pirate's Cove is a steep, overhanging bouldering alcove in the west section of Alderfer/Three Sisters Park, in the foothills near Evergreen, at roughly 7,500 feet. It sits close to Gilligan's Island, in an open meadow where many boulders catch direct sun. Fifteen problems are logged, all bouldering, spread from V0 up to a V10, with the middle of the range V4 to V5 and a couple of V7s. Overhanging lines dominate, though the rock quality is only so-so. A small pinnacle just left of the alcove holds a sloper-and-mantle test piece. Bring pads and a spotter; the walk from the larger lot is short.
